'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[American-led intervention in the Syrian civil war]]
**The [[United States Department of Defense]] reports that [[United States Air Force|forces]] have killed a senior [[al-Qaeda]] leader in [[Syria]] through an [[General Atomics MQ-9 Reaper|MQ-9]] [[drone strike]]. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/1953406/middle-east (AFP via ''Arab News'')]
*Assailants armed with guns and knives attack an [[Madrasa|Islamic seminary]] at [[Balukhali refugee camp]] for [[Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh|Rohingya refugees]] near the [[Bangladesh–Myanmar border]], killing seven people. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/22/bangladesh-rohingya-refugee-camps-seven-killed-police (Al Jazeera)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Evergrande liquidity crisis]]
**Chinese [[property developer]] [[Evergrande Group]] reports that it transferred [[United States dollar|US$]]83.5 million to pay off interests on its dollar bonds, allowing it to avert short-term [[Default (finance)|default]] a day before its deadline. [https://www.businessinsider.com/evergrande-repays-84-million-worth-of-interest-in-dollar-bonds-2021-10?amp (''Business Insider'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*At least 25 people are killed during an explosion and fire at an illegal [[oil refinery]] in [[Rivers State]], [[Nigeria]]. Children are among the victims. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/least-25-including-minors-died-illegal-refinery-blast-nigeria-2021-10-24/ (Reuters)]
*Sixteen people are killed and another is injured by an explosion at a [[chemical plant]] in [[Ryazan Oblast]], [[Russia]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/up-5-feared-dead-after-fire-russian-gunpowder-plant-reports-2021-10-22/ (Reuters)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iran]], [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on religion]]
****Mass [[Friday prayer|Friday prayers]] resume in the capital [[Tehran]] after a 20-month suspension due to the pandemic. Worshippers must adhere to [[social distancing]] measures and use [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic|face mask]]s during the gatherings, with most worshippers using their own prayer rugs and clay tablets. [https://english.alarabiya.net/coronavirus/2021/10/22/Friday-prayers-resume-in-Tehran-after-nearly-two-year-hiatus-due-to-COVID-19 (Al-Arabiya English)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in mainland China]]
****The Chinese capital [[Beijing]] begins administering [[booster dose]]s of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]]s to "at-risk" individuals over the age of 18, which includes those participating, organizing, or working in the [[2022 Winter Olympics]] as well as people working in education, manufacturing, retail, and public facilities. [https://thehill.com/policy/international/asia-pacific/577969-beijing-offering-booster-shots-ahead-of-winter-olympics (''The Hill'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Sri Lanka]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Sri Lanka]]
****[[President of Sri Lanka|President]] [[Gotabaya Rajapaksa]] orders [[Security guard|security personnel]] and [[healthcare worker|health care]] and tourism industry workers in [[Sri Lanka]] to receive a [[booster dose]] of the COVID-19 vaccine beginning on November 1 in order to revive the economy and specifically the tourism industry due to the effects of the pandemic. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/sri-lanka-orders-covid-19-booster-shots-frontline-workers-tourism-industry-2021-10-22/ (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Belarus]]
****[[Belarus]] ends its short-lived [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic|mask mandate]] that was introduced on October 9 despite a record number of COVID-19 cases as [[President of Belarus|President]] [[Alexander Lukashenko]] dismissed the measures as "unnecessary". [https://apnews.com/article/coronavirus-pandemic-europe-health-pandemics-belarus-23001be567f93f12980c60bedd81a77c (AP)] 
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports a record for the fourth consecutive day of 1,064 [[COVID-19 pandemic deaths|death]]s from COVID-19, bringing the nationwide death toll to 228,453. The country also reports a record for the second consecutive day of 37,141 new cases of COVID-19, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 8,168,305. [https://www.spa.gov.sa/viewfullstory.php?lang=en&newsid=2297583 (Saudi Press Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine]]
****[[Ukraine]] closes schools and public venues in [[Kyiv]] and will only permit the schools to reopen if teachers are vaccinated in other "red zone" areas after the country reported a record for the second consecutive day of 29,785 new cases and 614 deaths from COVID-19. [https://www.barrons.com/articles/ukraine-posts-record-covid-deaths-cases-for-second-day-01634890807 (AFP via ''Barron's'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Victoria]]
*****[[Melbourne]] lifts its world-record [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] restrictions as over 70% of the [[Victoria (Australia)|Victorian]] population are now fully [[COVID-19 vaccination in Australia|vaccinated]] against [[COVID-19]]. Private and public gatherings are now allowed with limitations and schools and businesses will reopen with density caps. The controversial night-time curfew is also lifted. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-10-21/victoria-melbourne-covid-lockdown-curfew-ends/100549690 (ABC News Australia)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Fiji]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Fiji]]
****After vaccinating most of its adult population, [[Fiji]] announces that it has already vaccinated 28,965 children between the ages of 15 and 17 with at least one dose of the COVID-19 vaccine. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/454061/fiji-vaccination-of-teens-going-strong (RNZ)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]]
****The [[New Zealand Government]] sets a target of 90% of the population fully vaccinated, which is very high by international standards, in order to end lockdown measures and shift to a new traffic light system giving [[COVID-19 vaccination in New Zealand|vaccinated]] [[Kiwi (people)|Kiwis]] more freedoms. https://www.1news.co.nz/2021/10/21/ardern-sets-covid-19-target-of-90-fully-vaccinated-to-ease-restrictions/ (1 News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Peru]]
***[[Peru]] surpasses 200,000 deaths from COVID-19, which is the second [[Latin America]]n country to do so after [[Brazil]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/peru-surpasses-200-000-coronavirus-deaths/2400487 (Anadolu Agency)]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
***[[Pfizer]] says that its vaccine is 90% [[Vaccine efficacy|effective]] in children between the ages of 5 and 11. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/pfizer-covid-vaccine-kids-effective-trials/ (CBS News)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2021 Eswatini protests]]
**Police and the army open fire on a group of health workers protesting outside a hospital in [[Eswatini]], injuring 30 people. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-59011033 (BBC News)]
*[[Murder of David Amess]]
**After appearing at [[Westminster Magistrates' Court]] and the [[Old Bailey]], Ali Harbi Ali is charged with the [[murder in English law|murder]] of [[David Amess]] and [[remand (detention)|remanded]] to [[Belmarsh]] prison. He is due to be tried on March 7, 2022. [https://bbc.co.uk/news/uk-59010500 (BBC News)] 
*[[Cannabis in Luxembourg]]
**[[Luxembourg]] legalizes cannabis, becoming the first country in Europe to do so. [https://www.thestreet.com/investing/luxembourg-first-eu-country-legalize-cannabis (TheStreet)]
*[[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]]
**The [[Ministry of Defense (Israel)|Israeli Defense Ministry]] designates six Palestinian groups, including human rights organization [[Al-Haq]] and non-profit organization [[Union of Agricultural Work Committees]], as "terrorist organisations" for their alleged connections to the [[Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine]]. The [[Palestinian National Authority]], the [[Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights]], and several human rights groups harshly criticize the designations. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/22/israel-palestinian-human-rights-groups-terrorism (Al Jazeera)]
